---
title: "Before Lesson 1"
---

Install Sonic Pi from [sonic-pi.net](https://sonic-pi.net/). The download page
covers macOS, Windows, Linux, and Raspberry Pi, and the installer is the whole
setup.

Open it, type this into the first buffer, and press **Run**.

```ruby
play 60
```

A note means you are ready.

Headphones or decent speakers do more for progress here than any other purchase,
because half of this course is hearing small differences. Laptop speakers
reproduce almost nothing below about 200 Hz, which is most of Part 1 and every
bass line in Part 10.

## Which version

Every example in this book was written and recorded against **Sonic Pi 5.0.0**.

Sonic Pi occasionally changes a synth default or a function signature between
releases. When a snippet sounds different from its recording, check the version
before assuming a typo. Help, About reports it, and so does
`Contents/Resources/VERSION` inside the application bundle on macOS.

Later versions will mostly behave identically. Earlier ones will not, and 5.0
introduced changes that the examples here rely on.

## The window

Three areas matter. The **buffers** hold your code, and there are ten of them,
which is more useful than it sounds once several voices are running. The **log**
on the right prints every note as it plays, and it is the first place to look
when something sounds wrong. The **help** pane at the bottom documents every
synth, sample, and function, and it is faster than searching the web.

Two shortcuts worth learning now: `Cmd-R` or `Alt-R` runs the buffer, and
`Cmd-.` or `Alt-.` stops everything.

## A first sound

Paste this in and run it. None of it needs to make sense yet. It is here so you
know what the destination sounds like.

```{.ruby audio="setup-1.mp3"}
# Four bars that already sound like music.
# Every construct here is explained by the end of Part 3.

use_bpm 96
use_synth :pluck

# E minor pentatonic. Five notes chosen so that any order sounds intentional.
melody = [:e4, :g4, :a4, :b4, :d5, :b4, :a4, :g4]

live_loop :tune do
  melody.each do |n|
    play n, release: 0.4
    sleep 0.25          # sixteenth notes at this tempo
  end
end

live_loop :bass do
  play :e2, release: 1.8, amp: 0.7, cutoff: 70
  sleep 2               # one bass note every two beats
end
```

Now change one thing. Set `melody` to `[:e4, :f4, :g4, :a4, :b4, :c5, :d5, :e5]`
and run it again. Same rhythm, same bass, different feeling. Working out why is
roughly what Parts 2 and 5 are for.

Press `Cmd-.` to stop it.
